Household employment rose by 406,000 while average hourly earnings increased just 0.1% in September, with the 12-month gain at 3%, the lowest since May 2021.
Market-implied odds that the Fed will hold rates steady at its October 27-28 meeting jumped to 82.8% according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Fed Vice Chairman Philip Jefferson said labor market conditions have stabilized with layoffs remaining low and job openings moving higher on net; wage growth has moderated with average hourly earnings expected to show 3.1% year-over-year increase in September, down from around 4% at the start of the year.

The Bureau of Economic Analysis adjusted methodology for measuring prices of legal services, software, computer accessories and portfolio management, lowering core July PCE by 0.36 percentage points.
Gross domestic product increased at a 2.2% annualized rate in Q2, revised up from 1.5%, with real final sales to private domestic purchasers up 4.6%.
Traders priced in less chance of a Fed rate hike in October following the report, with market expectations shifting the next expected increase to December.

key_facts: The personal consumption expenditures price index, the primary inflation gauge for the Federal Reserve, is expected to show increases of 0.3% at both all-items and core levels on Wednesday, with annual increases of 3.7% and 3.3% respectively, unchanged from July and well above the Fed's 2% target.

Fed officials at their September meeting approved a quarter percentage point rate increase and 16 of 18 Federal Open Market Committee officials indicated they expect at least one more rate move in 2026 as they raised their consensus PCE inflation outlook.

Fed Governor Michael Barr stated that tariffs and the prolonged war with Iran have knocked the Fed 'off course on our progress toward our 2% goal' and reiterated his belief that the Fed likely will need to continue to raise rates.

key_facts: The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index fell to 81.9 in September, down 6.7 points and below the Dow Jones consensus forecast of 89, marking the lowest level since 2014.
For the first time in the four-year history of the survey question, more respondents said their personal finances were bad as opposed to good.
Respondents expect an average inflation rate of 6.1%, up 0.3 percentage point from August, with median expectation rising 0.3 point to 5.1%.

The Present Situation Index fell 7.9 points to 109.3, while the Expectations Index slipped 5.9 points to 63.6; the jobs differential between 'plentiful' and 'hard to get' eroded to 1.7%, down 2.5 percentage points.
importance_reason: Sharp deterioration in consumer sentiment to 14-year lows reflects broad economic anxiety on inflation, labor market, and personal finances—a key forward-looking indicator of household spending and recession risk.

key_facts: The White House banned imports of Canadian vehicles, dairy and alcohol products on Tuesday, including motorcycles and mopeds with petrol engines larger than 800cc, whey products, molasses, and alcoholic beverages such as beer, cider, wine, whiskey and vodka. The products are estimated to total around $19.9 billion of Canadian imports by the American Action Forum.

President Trump stated he expected a 'fair deal' with Canada within coming weeks but maintained a combative tone, saying 'there's nothing they have that we need.' U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC there was 'no urgency on our side' to strike an agreement.

Canada imposed tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on 27.6 billion Canadian dollars ($19.45 billion) worth of U.S. goods including steel, dairy, agricultural equipment, paper, household appliances, furniture, clothing and electronics, described as a 'dollar for dollar' response to Washington's 50% tariffs imposed in August.

The Bank of Canada warned that new tariffs had made the country's growth prospects more uncertain and increased upside risks to inflation. The measures target a relatively small portion of the annual $715.5 billion trade in goods between the countries, but continued escalation is expected to significantly impact sectors such as metals and autos.

key_facts: Australia's central bank raised policy rates to 4.6%, the highest level in 15 years, with a 25 basis points hike to the cash rate in line with economist expectations.

The RBA has now raised rates four times this year by a total 100 basis points as inflation remains sticky, citing Middle East conflict broadening and global energy prices being much higher than assumed.
Australia's inflation hit a high of 4.6% in March and last came in at 3.5% in July, beating estimates, above the RBA's target band of 2%-3% for 2026.

The RBA stated it would continue to do what it considers necessary to contain inflation, including increasing the policy rate further, while warning of growth slowdown as rates rise with GDP growth at 2.1% in Q2 down from 2.5% in Q1.

market_link: RBA rate decision affects AUD/USD currency pair, ASX equity valuations, and mortgage costs; energy cost pass-through may influence regional commodity pricing.
